dataset.description:
This Data Management Plan (DMP) provides a full-lifecycle framework for managing research data generated by the doctoral project "AI-Assisted Information Behavior Patterns and Influencing Mechanisms among Chinese and Spanish Youth in Open Education" at Universidad Carlos III de Madrid.
The project employs a mixed-methods design and produces two types of primary data:
Quantitative survey data — structured questionnaire responses from approximately 800 young learners (400 in China, 400 in Spain), collected via Wenjuanxing and Qualtrics.
Qualitative interview data — audio recordings and text transcriptions from 40–50 semi-structured interviews with purposefully selected participants.
This DMP outlines how all data will be collected, processed, stored, shared, and preserved following the FAIR guiding principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). The anonymized survey data will be openly shared via Zenodo under a CC BY 4.0 license, while interview data containing personal and sensitive information will be kept under controlled access with openly available metadata (CC0). This approach ensures compliance with GDPR, research ethics requirements, and the Horizon Europe principle of "as open as possible, as closed as necessary."
This plan covers the full data lifecycle — from collection during 2026–2028 through long-term preservation for a minimum of 10 years after project completion — and serves as both a planning tool for the research team and a formal DMP deliverable for the doctoral programme.

distribution.available_until:
Anonymized survey data (open): Will remain publicly accessible in Zenodo for a minimum of 10 years after the end of the project, in line with Horizon Europe guidelines and UC3M data retention policy. Given that Zenodo is a long-term preservation repository, the data will remain available indefinitely unless there is a compelling reason for withdrawal.
Interview data (restricted): Metadata will remain publicly accessible for the same period. The restricted files will also be retained for a minimum of 10 years under controlled access. After this period, renewed ethical review will determine whether the data can remain accessible or should be securely destroyed by the repository.

metadata.description:
The following types of metadata will be created:
• Descriptive metadata: Title, authors, abstract, and keywords to enable data discovery.
• Administrative metadata: File formats, sizes, creation dates, and access conditions for data management.
• Structural metadata: Variable labels, coding schemes, and codebook documentation to help users understand the internal structure of the survey and interview data.
• Legal metadata: License information (CC BY 4.0 for open data, CC0 for metadata), data use agreements for controlled-access interview data, and ethics statements.

dataset.preservation_statement:
Long-term preservation is ensured through deposition in Zenodo, which provides:
Perpetual access: Zenodo is operated by CERN and funded by the European Commission with a commitment to long-term preservation.
Version control: All versions of datasets are preserved and remain accessible.
Persistent identifiers: DOIs ensure datasets remain findable even if storage infrastructure changes.
Metadata preservation: Metadata records (CC0) remain available even if data files become inaccessible.
File format migration: Data deposited in open formats (.csv, .txt) minimize the risk of format obsolescence.
